story.hook: My roommate charged me fake fees for months.
story.script:
When I moved into the apartment, my roommate told me the rent was split evenly. I never questioned it because the place was small, the rooms looked almost identical, and the total he quoted sounded normal for the area.

For the first few months, everything was fine. Then he created what he called a shared living spreadsheet. At first it was just electricity, internet, and cleaning supplies. Then strange charges started appearing. Ten dollars for sofa wear. Fifteen dollars because I had friends over twice in one month. Eight dollars for using more than half the fridge shelf. He even added a common area maintenance fee because I worked from the dining table on weekends.

I laughed the first time because I honestly thought it was a joke. He did not laugh back.

He told me he had been in the apartment longer, so he was basically the household manager. According to him, that meant he could decide what counted as extra usage. I refused to pay the new charges, and suddenly every conversation became about money. If I cooked, he mentioned gas. If I watched television, he mentioned electricity. If I left my shoes by the door, he called it storage in shared space.

Then one Friday he sent me an invoice for one hundred and forty-seven dollars and wrote, Please settle this with next month's rent.

That was the point where I stopped arguing and started checking.

I found our lease in the kitchen drawer. Both of our names were on it, and there was nothing about him being a household manager. More importantly, the lease listed the full monthly rent.

The number was lower than I expected.

I pulled up my bank transfers and did the math. For almost a year, I had been sending him exactly half of the amount he told me the apartment cost. But according to the actual lease, my transfers were covering much more than half.

So I emailed the landlord.

I kept the message simple. I said I wanted to confirm the rent amount and asked whether there were any approved household fees for furniture wear, common areas, or additional guests.

The landlord replied twenty minutes later.

There were no extra fees.

Then he added one sentence that made me read the email three times: For clarity, your roommate requested permission to collect rent from you directly, but the total rent has not changed since your tenancy began.

I sent back my transfer history.

The landlord called me immediately.

It turned out my roommate had been quietly making me pay several hundred dollars more than my actual share every month. The fake spreadsheet was not a new idea. It was just the first time he had tried to squeeze even more out of me in writing.

The landlord was furious, but not for the reason my roommate expected. Our lease required all tenants to be given accurate rent information, and the landlord had specifically warned him not to add unofficial charges.

That evening my roommate came home ready to argue about the one hundred and forty-seven dollars.

I was sitting at the dining table with the lease, my transfer records, and the landlord on speakerphone.

He went completely silent.

The landlord told him that from then on, each of us would pay our share directly. He also had to return the overpayment he had collected from me or the landlord would document the dispute formally and reconsider renewing his place on the lease.

My roommate tried to say the extra money covered administration.

The landlord asked, Administration of what?

There was a very long pause.

Two days later, the money started coming back to my account.

And that ridiculous one hundred and forty-seven dollar invoice? I printed it, highlighted the words common area maintenance fee, and kept it with my lease.

Because somehow, the guy who charged me for sitting at the dining table ended up paying me back from that exact same table.

youtube.title: My Roommate Invented Fees Until I Checked the Lease #Shorts
youtube.description: My roommate kept adding bizarre apartment fees until one lease check exposed a much bigger problem. An original Wacky Dramas story.
